why: Covers the 15 user-requested network shapes with inductors after V6 6/21 scale diagnostics.
method: V6 extended suffixes, corrected no-overlap placement, donor04 bridge inserted after first left wire for V0/G0.

cases.description: Inductor version of requested topology: A single resistor connected directly between the power terminal and ground.
Inductor version of requested topology: Four resistors connected end-to-end in one path from power to ground.
Inductor version of requested topology: Four resistors side-by-side, each connected from power to ground.
Inductor version of requested topology: A series resistor feeding a parallel group, then returning to ground.
Inductor version of requested topology: Two resistors in series between power and ground with one midpoint tap.
Inductor version of requested topology: Five series resistors creating four voltage tapping points.
Inductor version of requested topology: Five parallel resistors across power and ground to split current.
Inductor version of requested topology: Three resistors end-to-end forming a closed triangle between V0, D1, and G0.
Inductor version of requested topology: Three resistors sharing a central node, with outer nodes at power, ground, and an output terminal.
Inductor version of requested topology: A delta network and a star network side-by-side for comparison.
Inductor version of requested topology: Four-resistor diamond with power at top, ground at bottom, and side measurement nodes.
Inductor version of requested topology: Wheatstone bridge with equal ratios on both sides, plus high-value bridge measurement resistor.
Inductor version of requested topology: Wheatstone bridge with unequal side ratios and a bridge measurement resistor.
Inductor version of requested topology: Two vertical series branches with a fifth resistor bridging their middle joints.
Inductor version of requested topology: A four-step R-2R ladder using 1k and 2k resistor values.

notes: These files intentionally represent topology with terminal labels and short endpoint wires.
Physical triangle/star/bridge drawing is approximate; topology is carried by repeated net labels.
Stop at the first fatal Proteus error and report exact text plus the case id.
